questions.question: What are the tiny, grape-like air sacs that make up the lungs called?
options: Bronchioles
Alveoli
Capillaries
Tracheae

questions.question: Between which two structures does gas exchange take place in the human lungs?
options: Between the bronchi and the trachea
Between the air in alveoli and the blood in capillaries
Between the heart and the pulmonary vein
Between the ribs and the diaphragm

questions.question: Why does the human lung contain millions of alveoli instead of just one large air sac?
options: To decrease the overall lung volume
To increase the surface area of the lungs for gas exchange
To protect the lungs from physical damage
To warm up the incoming air more quickly

questions.question: How does the thickness of the alveoli walls adapt them for efficient gas exchange?
options: They are one cell thick to create a short diffusion distance
They are several cells thick to withstand high pressure
They are covered in a thick layer of mucus to trap oxygen
They are made of thick muscle tissue to pump gases

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the rich network of capillaries surrounding the alveoli?
options: To keep the alveoli at a high temperature
To maintain a concentration gradient for gas exchange
To physically support the delicate shape of the alveoli
To produce mucus to clean the lungs

questions.question: Which gas is an essential reactant required for aerobic cellular respiration to take place?
options: Carbon dioxide
Nitrogen
Oxygen
Hydrogen

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct word equation for aerobic cellular respiration?
options: Glucose + Oxygen -> Carbon dioxide + Water (+ Energy)
Glucose -> Lactic acid (+ Energy)
Glucose + Carbon dioxide -> Oxygen + Water (+ Energy)
Carbon dioxide + Water -> Glucose + Oxygen

questions.question: In which cellular structures does aerobic cellular respiration take place in animal, plant, and fungi cells?
options: Only in the nucleus
In the mitochondria and cytoplasm
Only in the chloroplasts
In the cell wall and vacuole

questions.question: Why do active muscle cells contain significantly more mitochondria than fat storage cells?
options: They need to store more fat molecules
They require more energy because they do a lot of work
They need to produce more carbon dioxide for excretion
They are larger and need physical support

questions.question: What are the products of anaerobic cellular respiration in microorganisms like yeast?
options: Lactic acid and water
Carbon dioxide and ethanol
Oxygen and glucose
Carbon dioxide and lactic acid

questions.question: What is another name for anaerobic cellular respiration in microorganisms?
options: Photosynthesis
Fermentation
Transpiration
Aeration

questions.question: During strenuous exercise in humans, anaerobic cellular respiration can occur. What product does it build up that can cause muscle cramps?
options: Ethanol
Lactic acid
Carbon dioxide
Glucose

questions.question: Where inside a cell does anaerobic cellular respiration take place?
options: Only in the mitochondria
Only in the cytoplasm, without involving the mitochondria
In both the mitochondria and the nucleus
Inside the ribosomes

questions.question: How does the energy release of anaerobic cellular respiration compare to aerobic cellular respiration?
options: It provides more energy, but much more slowly
It provides less energy, but provides energy more quickly
It provides the same amount of energy at the same rate
It provides no energy at all

questions.question: Which of the following describes cellular respiration?
options: The physical movement of chest muscles to draw air into the lungs
A chemical process that uses glucose from food as a fuel to provide energy
The absorption of oxygen through the skin
The transport of digested food through the bloodstream

questions.question: When and in which living things does cellular respiration happen?
options: Only in animals during the daytime
Only in plants when there is no sunlight
In all living organisms all the time
Only in humans when they are exercising

questions.question: What is meant by the 'vital capacity' of the lungs?
options: The volume of air that remains in the lungs after a normal breath
The maximum volume of air that can be exhaled after inhaling fully
The total amount of oxygen absorbed by the blood in one minute
The average volume of air inhaled during quiet breathing
